title: ENGINEER - Materials Science and Failure Analysis

cond_0001.intro: The Materials Science and Failure Analysis Section develops solutions for complex materials problems using experimental and analytical methods. We serve government and commercial sponsors across a variety of technical sectors.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Objectives of this Role:**
Provide laboratory support for research projects involving materials synthesis, optimization, and failure analysis. Use a variety of chemical/physical processes for materials synthesis and bench top characterization techniques to evaluate material systems. Provide data analysis and present results from project tasks in person and in writing to a multidisciplinary project team. Assist in, or lead, the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses, including electronic, thermal, and mechanical controls.
Daily and Monthly Responsibilities:**
With guidance from senior staff, perform analytical and experimental work in materials science and chemistry laboratory spaces. As necessary, perform troubleshooting on experimental methods and data acquisition instruments. Analyze and summarize collected data utilizing multiple post processing tools and report data to project team. Support or lead the design and assembly of specialized laboratory apparatuses. Coordinate with other operating groups to fulfill project needs.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:**
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or Materials Science & Engineering.
0–3 Years hands-on experience operating laboratory analytical instruments, related to chemistry or materials characterization.
Strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills, ability to work independently, and ability to communicate complex information effectively.
A valid/clear driver's license.
Applicant must be a U.S. Citizen and able to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information following a government security investigation.
Preferred Requirements:**
0–2 Years hands-on experience with LabVIEW or similar control engineering software, or programming languages (Fortran, Python, etc.).
0–2 Years hands-on experience in the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses, including familiarity with CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks), process flow diagramming, and electrical and mechanical control systems.

We serve government and commercial sponsors across a variety of technical sectors. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of materials behavior and experimental methods.
cond_0013.responsibilities:
Objectives of this Role:**
Provide laboratory support for research projects involving materials synthesis, optimization, and failure analysis. Use a variety of chemical/physical processes for materials synthesis and bench top characterization techniques to evaluate material systems. Provide data analysis and present results from project tasks in person and in writing to a multidisciplinary project team. Assist in, or lead, the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses, including electronic, thermal, and mechanical controls.
Daily and Monthly Responsibilities:**
With guidance from senior staff, perform analytical and experimental work in materials science and chemistry laboratory spaces. As necessary, perform troubleshooting on experimental methods and data acquisition instruments. Analyze and summarize collected data utilizing multiple post processing tools and report data to project team. Support or lead the design and assembly of specialized laboratory apparatuses. Coordinate with other operating groups to fulfill project needs.
cond_0013.requirements:
Requires a Bachelors degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering.
0-3 Years: Hands-on experience operating laboratory analytical instruments, preferably related to chemistry or materials characterization.
0-3 Years: Must possess strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills, the ability to work independently and effectively communicate complex information.
0-2 Years: Hands on experience with LabVIEW or similar control engineering software, programming languages (Fortran, Python, etc.) is desired.
0-2 Years: Hands on experience in the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses. Familiarity with CAD software (e.g., Solid Works), processes flow diagraming, electrical and mechanical control systems is desired.
A valid/clear driver's license is required.
Special Requirements:**
Applicant selected will be subject to a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. Applicant must be a U.S. Citizen.

cond_0159.responsibilities:
Provide laboratory support for research projects involving materials synthesis, optimization, and failure analysis. Use a variety of chemical/physical processes for materials synthesis and bench top characterization techniques to evaluate material systems. Regularly share data analysis and present results from project tasks in person and in writing to a multidisciplinary project team. Assist in, or lead, the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses, including electronic, thermal, and mechanical controls.
With guidance from senior staff, perform analytical and experimental work in materials science and chemistry laboratory spaces. As necessary, perform troubleshooting on experimental methods and data acquisition instruments. Analyze and summarize collected data utilizing multiple post processing tools and report data to the project team. Support or lead the design and assembly of specialized laboratory apparatuses. Stay in regular contact with other operating groups to fulfill project needs.

0-2 Years: Hands on experience with LabVIEW or similar control engineering software, programming languages (Fortran, Python, etc.) is desired.
0-2 Years: Hands on experience in the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses. Familiarity with CAD software (e.g., Solid Works), processes flow diagraming, electrical and mechanical control systems is desired.

cond_0350.intro: The Materials Science and Failure Analysis Section develops solutions for complex materials problems using experimental and analytical methods. We serve government and commercial sponsors across a variety of technical sectors.
cond_0350.responsibilities:
Own laboratory support for research projects involving materials synthesis, optimization, and failure analysis. Execute a variety of chemical/physical processes for materials synthesis and benchtop characterization techniques to evaluate material systems. Deliver data analysis and present results from project tasks in person and in writing to a multidisciplinary project team. Lead or direct the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses, including electronic, thermal, and mechanical controls.
With guidance from senior staff, execute analytical and experimental work in materials science and chemistry laboratory spaces. As necessary, take ownership of troubleshooting experimental methods and data acquisition instruments. Analyze and summarize collected data utilizing multiple post-processing tools and report data to the project team. Lead or drive the design and assembly of specialized laboratory apparatuses. Direct coordination with other operating groups to fulfill project needs.
cond_0350.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or Materials Science & Engineering.
Hands-on experience operating laboratory analytical instruments, related to chemistry or materials characterization (0–3 years).
Strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills, ability to work independently, and ability to communicate complex information effectively (0–3 years).
Valid/clear driver's license.
Applicant must be a U.S. Citizen and able to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information following a government security investigation.
Preferred Requirements
Hands-on experience with LabVIEW or similar control engineering software, or programming languages such as Fortran or Python (0–2 years).
Hands-on experience in the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses; familiarity with CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks), process flow diagramming, and electrical and mechanical control systems (0–2 years).

cond_0450.intro: The Materials Science and Failure Analysis Section develops solutions for complex materials problems using experimental and analytical methods. We serve government and commercial sponsors across a variety of technical sectors.
cond_0450.responsibilities:
Objectives of this Role:
Support research projects involving materials synthesis, optimization, and failure analysis, working alongside a multidisciplinary team. Use a variety of chemical and physical processes for materials synthesis and benchtop characterization techniques to evaluate material systems. Share data analysis results with the project team through written reports and in-person presentations. Assist in or coordinate the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses, including electronic, thermal, and mechanical controls.
Daily and Monthly Responsibilities:
With guidance from senior staff, contribute to analytical and experimental work in materials science and chemistry laboratory spaces. As needed, work with the team to troubleshoot experimental methods and data acquisition instruments. Analyze and summarize collected data using multiple post-processing tools and share findings with the project team. Support or help coordinate the design and assembly of specialized laboratory apparatuses. Coordinate with other operating groups to fulfill project needs.
cond_0450.requirements:
Requires a Bachelors degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering.
0-3 Years: Hands-on experience operating laboratory analytical instruments, preferably related to chemistry or materials characterization.
0-3 Years: Must possess strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills, the ability to work independently and effectively communicate complex information.
0-2 Years: Hands on experience with LabVIEW or similar control engineering software, programming languages (Fortran, Python, etc.) is desired.
0-2 Years: Hands on experience in the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses. Familiarity with CAD software (e.g., Solid Works), processes flow diagraming, electrical and mechanical control systems is desired.
A valid/clear driver's license is required.
Special Requirements:
Applicant selected will be subject to a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. Applicant must be a U.S. Citizen.

cond_0549.intro: The Materials Science and Failure Analysis Section develops solutions for complex materials problems using experimental and analytical methods. We collaborate with government and commercial sponsors across a variety of technical sectors.
cond_0549.responsibilities:
Objectives of this Role:
Support research projects involving materials synthesis, optimization, and failure analysis, working alongside a multidisciplinary team. Help apply a variety of chemical and physical processes for materials synthesis and benchtop characterization to evaluate material systems. Contribute to data analysis and share results from project tasks — in person and in writing — with the broader project team. Assist in or coordinate the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses, including electronic, thermal, and mechanical controls.
Daily and Monthly Responsibilities:
With guidance from senior staff, carry out analytical and experimental work in materials science and chemistry laboratory spaces. As needed, work with the team to troubleshoot experimental methods and data acquisition instruments. Analyze and summarize collected data using multiple post-processing tools and share findings with the project team. Support or help coordinate the design and assembly of specialized laboratory apparatuses. Work alongside other operating groups to help fulfill project needs.
cond_0549.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or Materials Science & Engineering
Hands-on experience operating laboratory analytical instruments, related to chemistry or materials characterization (0–3 years)
Strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and communicate complex information clearly (0–3 years)
Valid/clear driver's license
Applicant must be a U.S. Citizen and able to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information following a government security investigation
Preferred Requirements:
Hands-on experience with LabVIEW or similar control engineering software, or programming languages such as Fortran or Python (0–2 years)
Hands-on experience in the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses; familiarity with CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks), process flow diagramming, and electrical/mechanical control systems (0–2 years)

Provide laboratory support for research projects involving materials synthesis, optimization, and failure analysis. Use a variety of chemical/physical processes for materials synthesis and bench top characterization techniques to evaluate material systems. Provide data analysis and present results from project tasks in person and in writing to a multidisciplinary project team. Assist in, or lead, the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses, including electronic, thermal, and mechanical controls.

With guidance from senior staff, perform analytical and experimental work in materials science and chemistry laboratory spaces. Coordinate with other operating groups to fulfill project needs.

0-3 Years: Hands-on experience operating laboratory analytical instruments, preferably related to chemistry or materials characterization.
0-3 Years: Must possess strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills, the ability to work independently and effectively communicate complex information.
0-2 Years: Hands on experience with LabVIEW or similar control engineering software, programming languages (Fortran, Python, etc.) is desired.
0-2 Years: Hands on experience in the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses. Familiarity with CAD software (e.g., Solid Works), processes flow diagraming, electrical and mechanical control systems is desired.
A valid/clear driver's license is required.

Applicant selected will be subject to a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. Applicant must be a U.S. Citizen.

cond_0641.intro: The Materials Science and Failure Analysis Section develops solutions for complex materials problems using experimental and analytical methods. We serve government and commercial sponsors across a variety of technical sectors.
cond_0641.responsibilities:
Objectives of this Role:**
Provide laboratory support for research projects involving materials synthesis, optimization, and failure analysis. Use a variety of chemical/physical processes for materials synthesis and bench top characterization techniques to evaluate material systems. Provide data analysis and present results from project tasks in person and in writing to a multidisciplinary project team. Assist in, or lead, the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses, including electronic, thermal, and mechanical controls.
Daily and Monthly Responsibilities:**
With guidance from senior staff, perform analytical and experimental work in materials science and chemistry laboratory spaces. As necessary, perform troubleshooting on experimental methods and data acquisition instruments. Analyze and summarize collected data utilizing multiple post processing tools and report data to project team. Support or lead the design and assembly of specialized laboratory apparatuses. Coordinate with other operating groups to fulfill project needs.
cond_0641.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or Materials Science & Engineering required; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Demonstrated expertise operating laboratory analytical instruments, preferably related to chemistry or materials characterization.
Proven track record of strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and effectively communicate complex information.
Solid proficiency with LabVIEW or similar control engineering software and programming languages (Fortran, Python, etc.).
Deep knowledge of the design and assembly of laboratory apparatuses, with strong command of CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks), process flow diagramming, and electrical and mechanical control systems.
A valid/clear driver's license is required.
Special Requirements:**
Applicant selected will be subject to a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. Applicant must be a U.S. Citizen.
